newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India GDRs easier on thin volumes.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India GDRs easier on thin volumes.

text.p: Indian global depository receipts (GDRs) eased again on Tuesday, extending losses amid a lack of interest following mild declines in Bombay, traders said.
They said the market had mirrored sluggish trade in India, where dealers see a consolidation following recent post-budget gains.
A GDR trader said prices had eased on thin volumes, with little selling pressure seen.
Reliance and SBI both managed mild gains in an easier market, but Indian Hotels and Hindalco both shed 50 cents to $30/$31 and $22.35/23.35 respectively.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.71 points lower, a 0.94 percent fall to 75.07, while the premium over the local market slipped to 15.59 percent from 16.56 percent on Monday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index shed 2.95 points to 3,795.17.

In other Asian markets, the Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.22 points at 116.03 following steep gains on Monday. Prices were at a 0.03 percent premium to the local market, which made 1.18 percent on Tuesday.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.05 percent higher at 58.83, a 0.03 point rise. The premium was 42.94 percent.
